limitations: Name and revision grouping is conservative but heuristic; manual family adjudication is required before freezing a split.
Load-verification metadata establishes only the recorded smoke/load check, not full-match fidelity or strategic suitability.
A lack of settings/source references does not prove that the author never viewed, played, or tuned against a map.
Tier B is a path-based evidence classification: only explicitly enumerated upstream/administrative sources are non-adaptive, and all ambiguity defaults to disqualifying.
An administrative-only reference does not prove that a map was unseen by the author.
INI dimensions, theater, and waypoint descriptors are metadata only; no map geometry or gameplay was evaluated.
Only map files under the configured driver data root are cataloged.

scope.evidenceBasedEligibilityPolicy: Historical settings or adaptive-development references make the family ineligible. Explicit upstream inventory, upstream documentation, and outcome-blind catalog references are recorded but do not alone disqualify.
scope.experimentEvidencePolicy: Read settings.maps only from experiment_inventory.jsonl; episode, evaluation, checkpoint, and match-result files are not opened.
scope.familyPolicy: Connected components over exact SHA-256, normalized names, normalized known-revision names, and explicit provenance raw/compatibility aliases.
scope.referenceClassificationDefault: Any unclassified or ambiguous project source is adaptive and disqualifying; only enumerated administrative/upstream sources are non-adaptive.
scope.strictEligibilityPolicy: Any historical settings use or any textual source/config reference makes the entire connected family ineligible.
scope.textReferenceCorpusPolicy: Root configuration/README files, package config and src trees, and research configs/scripts/slurm/tests; data, research reports/artifacts, benchmark-results, node_modules, and build outputs are excluded.
